key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power and current intensify molten-pool convection and penetration, while higher travel speed reduces heat input and shrink weld size but can destabilize the arc.
engineering_relevance: The results provide process-window guidance for improving joint quality and arc stability when welding low-thermal-expansion Invar components for aerospace mold applications.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool flow and morphology evolution
High-speed photography of arc behavior during laser-TIG hybrid welding
Parameter sweep over laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent trends across 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min welding speed, and 150–170 A current, linking each parameter to penetration depth, weld width, flow intensity, and arc shape/stability.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a limited parameter range, so transfer to different joint geometries, thicknesses, or shielding conditions should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
